page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, configured as 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 1.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-highcpu-2 operates in lower performance tiers across multiple workloads. In stress-ng testing, it achieved a single-core score of 1399.29 and a multi-core score of 1841.88. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 102.26 GB/sec, which drops to 13.72 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and integer execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and AES, though Passmark CPU encryption tests recorded a score of 839.13.

Given its low memory allocation of 1.0 GB per core and poor multi-core benchmark results, this instance is constrained for memory-intensive or highly parallelized applications. It is best suited for lightweight, compute-focused tasks that do not require significant memory overhead, such as basic text processing, simple single-threaded utilities, or low-traffic static web serving.
